name: Alfred le Fermier - 2025 ACS Best in Show!
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromagerie la Station - Quebec, Canada
description: Fromagerie la Station’s journey to award-winning cheesemaking began with Alfred and Aglaé Bolduc’s 1928 arrival to the town of Compton in Québec province. Four generations later, the Bolduc family is still working the same land, now making farmstead organic cheeses and harvesting maple syrup. Best in Show winner at the American Cheese Society’s 2025 competition, Alfred le Fermier has a sunset yellow rind and a woodsy aroma. Alfred’s notes of floral honey, fruit, and hazelnut as well as its yielding texture make it ideal for melting, slicing onto sandwiches, or snacking.

name: Raclette de Compton au Poivre - 2024 ACS Best in Show!
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromagerie la Station - Quebec, Canada
description: Fromagerie la Station’s journey to award-winning cheesemaking began with Alfred and Aglaé Bolduc’s 1928 arrival to the town of Compton in Québec province. Four generations later, the Bolduc family is still working the same land, now making farmstead organic cheeses and harvesting maple syrup. Best in Show winner at the American Cheese Society’s 2024 competition, Raclette de Compton au Poivre has a copper-colored washed rind, a supple golden paste, and a line of pink peppercorns running through the center of the cheese. The aromas of apple, chestnut, and butter open even more when heated. Perfect for melting over boiled potatoes, crusty bread, cornichons, and cured meats!

name: Staff Pick - Cow's Milk
tagline: You choose the texture & the flavor, we'll choose the cheese!
description: If you are reading this, you like cow's milk cheese. Well, we do too! Here's all you do: just choose the texture, flavor & the amount and we'll do the rest! Based on your answers, we'll choose a cheese that we love and that fits your criteria - couldn't be easier! It's just like standing in front of the cheese case! Feel free to add any specifics in the Instructions/Additions field at checkout. The published price per lb is only a place holder - the exact price of the cheese will be determined by the amount selected and the actual price per lb.

name: Morbier AOP
tagline: Raw Cow - Jean Perrin - Cleron, France
description: Welcome back, Morbier! After a 9-year absence from the US, we are delighted to have authentic Morbier back in our case. This legendary cheese from the Jura mountains dates back to the late nineteenth century. Farmers would typically deliver their milk to the village cheese dairy to make Comte. However, in the winter when travel was more difficult and cows produce less milk, they would make their own smaller-format cheese on the farm. The curd made from the morning milking would be dusted in a layer of ash to protect it until finishing the process with curd from the following morning. These days Morbier’s distinctive line of ash through the center is more for tradition than anything else. This supple cheese delivers notes of yogurt, caramel, and fruit, developing roasted, spicy, and vegetal nuances as it ages. Morbier is a striking addition to a cheese board and it also melts wonderfully. Try using it as raclette or in the gratin known as morbiflette, a variation of tartiflette.

name: Shadow Blossom
tagline: Raw Cow - Hofkaserei Kraus/Restaurant Schattbuch - Allgau, Germany
description: Shadow Blossom is a product of the mutual admiration between cheesemaker Albert Kraus and Michelin starred Restaurant Schattbuch. After a lot of "talking shop" together during a few dinners, they came up with this cheese. Starting from a traditional Allgäu semi-hard cheese, they coat the rind with Wild Madagascar pepper, Long Pepper, tailed pepper, kampot pepper, pink berries and cardamom. Pleasantly soft and crunchy in texture, creamy and buttery in taste, with the kick and complex flavors of six different pepper varieties!

name: Le Cousin
tagline: Raw Cow - Schmidhauser - Haute Savoie, France
description: Family first they say...this cheese is true to the mantra. A border-crossing cheese, named Le Cousin after the cousin, Jurg, whose dairy produces this wonderful alpine cheese before it is moved to the Haute Savoie dairy (France) where it is aged 6 more months. A semi-firm, fruity cheese with a sweetly salty tang, it is great for melting a fondue or grilled cheese! Fun Fact: The paper label that is placed on every finished wheel has both cousins adorned in the their respective Swiss or French garb. Great outfits, great cheese!

name: OG Kristal
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Van Tricht - Roeselare, Belgium
description: This assertive Belgian gouda is a must-try cheese for any lover of tyrosine crystals. What are those? Glad you asked…they are the crunchy, salty, savory bits of amino acid that form in aged cheeses as the protein structure of the milk breaks down. Yes, those! Chances are you have enjoyed them before! Like many aged goudas, the base flavor of OG Kristal leans sweeter, with notes of boozy cherries and butterscotch. The crystallized texture provides a savory balance to the fruity, nutty sweetness.

name: Brabander
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Fromagerie L'Amuse/Essex St. Cheese Co. - Netherlands
description: Goat cheese meets aged gouda. Brabander embodies the most beloved qualities of both. Made from the milk of the Saanen goats in the Brabant region of southern Holland, Brabander is aged for six months by famed affineur Betty Koster at Fromagerie L'Amuse. Its porcelain-colored paste is buttery and creamy with a lasting finish of sweet caramel.

name: Challerhocker
tagline: Raw Cow - Käserei Tufertschwil/Chas & Co. - Lütisburg, Switzerland
description: Pronunciation: "hollar hocker." Translation: "sitting in the cellar." Originally an Appenzeller maker, Walter Rass began experimenting and fine-tuning recipes to create this remarkable cheese - the result is truly special. It is washed in wine and spices and aged for a minimum of 10 months. Deep in flavor with a slight fruitiness, it is firm yet creamy, with notes of roasted nuts and butterscotch.

name: Comte - Aged 24 Months
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromageries Vagne - Franche-Comte, France
description: This Comté is made using summer milk from the iconic French dairy cow breed Montbéliarde and then aged for two years by traditional cheesemakers in Eastern France. The end result is all the nutty flavors of Alpine cheeses that you love but kicked up a notch with a sublte fruitiness and a slight, yeasty sweetness. The longer aging process results in a scattering of tyrosine throughout the paste of this cheese - those crunchy crystals that make a cheese addictively snackable. This makes an excellent addition to fondue but is also delicious to munch on in it's pure form. Pair this with green apples, green grapes, or skip the fruit and pour yourself a glass of crisp, white wine!

name: Comte, aged 5-7 months
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromageries Vagne - Franche-Comte, France
description: Comte is unquestionably one of our favorite and most versatile cheeses on the planet. With layers and layers of flavors, it can be enjoyed when young or aged. Aged between 5-7 months, this version is a pliable, nutty, fruity comte with great melting properties. Perfect for everything from snacking to sandwiches to fondue.

name: Fontina Val d'Aosta
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromagerie Haut Val'Ayas - Piedmont, Italy
description: Often imitated, never duplicated - Fontina Val d'Aosta is the original Italian fontina. It is semi-firm & creamy, with a washed rind that imparts a mildly pungent aroma. Flavors are rich and nutty with a subtle hint of fruit and grass. One of the world's greatest melting cheeses, it is the centerpiece to Piedmont's famous fonduta - a silky blend of Fontina val D'Aosta, cream, eggs, and shaved white truffle. Also fantastic on a sandwich with prosciutto, or added to mozzarella on a pizza.

name: Gruyere 1655
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromagerie le Cret - Fribourg, Switzerland
description: Master Cheesemaker Jean-Marie Dunand runs the village dairy at 3,000 ft above sea level in the heartland of traditional Gruyère production in the Fribourg region of Switzerland. The dairy, which dates back to 1900, has been run by Dunand since 1986. He makes 18-20 wheels of Gruyère each day, 365 days a year, using freshly delivered milk from eight small local farms. After three months, the wheels are moved to the caves of Fromage Gruyère, where they are finished aging for the next 9 months before release. Each wheel is rigorously evaluated by an expert team before earning the 1655 label. The result is a cheese that is perfectly balanced. Sweet, salty, nutty, fruity, mushroomy and earthy.

name: Gruyere AOP Classic
tagline: Raw Cow - Le Superbe - Fribourg, Switzerland
description: Produced since 1115 in the area surrounding the little village of Gruyère in western Switzerland, this much-loved cheese is still made in local dairies according to the original traditional recipe. With its buttery, caramel flavor and ultra-creamy texture, it is one of the most popular cheeses in our case. Aged about 6 months, it is suitable for your cheese board, but also incredibly versatile in the kitchen. One of the world's great melting cheeses, it is perfect for fondue, quiche or grilled sandwiches.

name: L'Amuse Gouda
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Cono/Fromagerie L'Amuse/Essex St. Cheese Co. - Netherlands
description: L’Amuse Signature Gouda is the product of a close collaboration between several gouda producers, mainly Cono and Lutjewinkel, in the Beemster and Schermer region and Betty Koster, owner of L’Amuse cheese store, near Amsterdam in the Netherlands. Wheels are carefully graded and selected before being transferred to a warehouse where they are tended and matured at the cellars for up to 30 months before being released and sold. Koster matures these goudas at higher temperatures (51-54 F) and humidity levels higher than normal which allows the crystals to form while preserving the moist, buttery paste and nutty flavor. Bright orange in color with a thick wax rind, L'Amuse Gouda is hard and dense with flavors of butterscotch, caramel and hazelnuts.

name: Schnebelhorn
tagline: Raw Cow - Reto Guntensperger & Kaserei Butschwil - Saint Gallen, Switzerland
description: Schnebelhorn is made with raw milk which comes from Swiss Brown / Braunvieh cows. Its creator, Reto Güntensperger, is a third-generation cheesemaker in the canton of St. Gallen. His grandfather made Appenzeller, his father made Appenzeller, but Reto wants to branch out. When the Swiss Cheese Union collapsed in 1999, he had his chance. Cream enriched & aged for 8 months, it has aromas of toasted hazelnuts, brown butter & roasted onions. The paste is firm & pale gold, with flecks of crystals & a creamy finish.

name: Smoked Gouda
description: This mild and creamy gouda is produced in Northern Holland. It then travels to the USA to be slowly smoked over smoldering oakwood chips. The final product is velvety and silky with a dark, smoky rind. The paste maintains the rich creaminess of Gouda, but with subtle smoky undertones. For some reason, smoked gouda always makes us think of hiking and camping. It's fantastic with cooked and cured meats, on sandwiches or even as a burger topping.

name: Supreme des Alpes Signature
tagline: Thermised Cow - Moleson Signature - Friboug, Switzerland
description: Suprême des Alpes (supreme of the Alps) is a Swiss cheese made in the same style as Gruyère and Vacherin Fribourgeois. Made in copper cauldrons, Suprême des Alpes is the result of a collaboration between Fromi’s Master Cheesemaker and the Fromagerie Moléson. Under the rustic natural rind, the cheese is smooth, dense and compact with some small tyrosine crystals forming over the 12-month maturation. The interior has a sweet-savory aroma with hints of tropical fruit and broth, and a rich flavor of roasted nuts, sweet cream and alpine herbs. Perfect on its own or as a welcome addition to fondue!

name: Twisca
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Treur Kaas - Winkel, Netherlands
description: Twisca is a delicious and flavorful sheep milk gouda made in North Holland. This cheese owes its full, creamy taste to the meadows where the sheep are free to graze. The salty, wetland environment makes the grass in these meadows richer and the milk (and cheese made with that milk) much more complex. Twisca offers a savory nuttiness, balanced by a smooth texture. Delicious and infinitely pairable, it's a crowd pleaser that's sure to delight even the pickiest eater!
